question.text: Which of the following is TRUE about the Direct Plan of a mutual fund scheme?

answer.text: Direct Plan has a different fund manager than Regular Plan
Direct Plan invests in different securities than Regular Plan
Direct Plan and Regular Plan differ in total expense ratio due to distribution expenses
Direct Plan is only available to institutional investors

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that Direct Plan and Regular Plan of the same scheme differ in their total expense ratio because the Direct Plan does not include distribution expenses and commission. Both plans share the same portfolio and fund manager but carry separate NAVs reflecting the difference in expenses. The Trap: Direct Plan is available to all investors, not only institutions. The difference between the two plans is in the expense ratio and the resulting NAV, not in the portfolio, fund manager, or risk. Note: Investors who prefer guidance from a distributor may opt for the Regular Plan; those who invest directly through the AMC can choose the Direct Plan and benefit from the lower TER.
